content.title: MLB on NBC: Sunday Night Baseball & Sunday Leadoff Broadcast Team, Explained
content.text: Spring is already in the air in many parts of the country, and that means baseball season can't be far behind. On March 26, Major League Baseball returns for 2026 Opening Day, which also means the long-awaited return of baseball to NBC Sports. How to WatchWatch Sunday Night Baseball on NBC and Peacock.With MLB coming to NBC and Peacock, that means the launch of two shows: the MLB Sunday Leadoff pregame show and, of course, Sunday Night Baseball, the primetime spotlight that'll bring you some of the biggest games in the league. We're just weeks away from its debut, so ahead of baseball's return, let's take a closer look at the voices who'll be bringing you each broadcast. RELATED: Major League Baseball Leagues and Divisions, ExplainedWho's calling Sunday Night Baseball for NBC?As with Sunday Night Football and Sunday Night Basketball, NBC's Sunday Night Baseball will bring together seasoned professional sports broadcasters with years of experience alongside MLB legends, who'll be there to provide expert commentary and context on each game, player, and new development in the season. Let's take a closer look at the team. Bob CostasA sports broadcasting icon who's covered the NBA Finals, World Series, Olympic Games, and beyond, Bob Costas returns to NBC this season after years of calling baseball elsewhere. He'll bring his decades of wisdom and experience to the program as the host of Sunday Night Baseball, handling Sunday Leadoff duties as well as features and other elements of the broadcast. Jason Benetti A 15-year veteran of MLB broadcasting, Jason Benetti returns to NBC after several years calling baseball elsewhere, including being the TV voice of the Detroit Tigers. He previously called MLB and Olympic baseball for NBC Sports. Now he'll act as the lead play-by-play announcer for Sunday Night Baseball, joined each week by a rotating roster of analysts, each with their own connections to the teams on the diamond. Ahmed FareedA three-time Emmy winner and versatile broadcaster and host, NBC Sports viewers have seen Ahmed Fareed do everything from hosting Olympics coverage to covering baseball, basketball, hockey, horse racing, soccer, and more. Now, while also handling Monday night NBA on NBC hosting duties at Peacock, he'll be hosting Sunday Night Leadoff, guiding viewers through the state of the MLB in the leadup to each primetime game. RELATED: When is MLB Opening Day for the 2026 Season?Clayton KershawFollowing his retirement at the end of the 2025 season, which earned him a third World Series title as a member of the Los Angeles Dodgers, Kershaw joins NBC Sports this season as an expert analyst. One of the greatest pitchers of his generation, he's a three-time Cy Young Award winner, an 11-time All-Star, and a Roberto Clemente Award Winner. Joey VottoA legend in Cincinnati, Votto spent 17 season as a member of the Reds, during which he earned six All-Star selections, a Gold Glove award as a first baseman, and the 2010 National League MVP. Now, he brings his knowledge, and the charisma that made him a fan-favorite, to the Sunday Night Baseball crew.Anthony RizzoA member of the Chicago Cubs 2016 World Series team, which broke more than a century of championship droughts for the club, Anthony Rizzo is a three-time All-Star, four-time Gold Glove winner, and Platinum Glove winner who, in 14 seasons, developed a reputation as a reliable slugger. He played for three different legendary teams, and his work with his own nonprofit foundation for cancer research earned him a Roberto Clemente Award for community service excellence among baseball players.Who's Calling MLB Sunday Leadoff?Matt VasgersianMatt Vasgersian is a veteran MLB play-by-play voice and host, and will be handling play-by-play for many of the MLB Sunday Leadoff games for NBC Sports. He has been a baseball commentator for decades, and returns to NBC Sports after calling MLB Sunday Leadoff games for Peacock in 2023. He also worked five Olympic Games for NBC Sports, including calling baseball and softball games as part of that assignment. Fans might also recognize his voice from the MLB The Show video game franchise, which featured Vasgersian in the 2006-2021 installments.
